extraction.topic: GOAL_ALFRED.md A-0803 (Supersession): the real Snowflow-boot architectural switch at commit ec32657
extraction.retrieval_anchor: CLAUDE.md 'Status: two subsystems, one repo' section
extraction.notes: A real, already-documented supersession event: commit ec3265749dd2648d74327bbc51ef8d21648a0c88 ('Drop in Snowflow as SHADED's runtime appearance (1:1 import)') changed index.html's boot chain from the direct runtime/*.mjs engine to /src/main.js (Snowflow). CLAUDE.md's own status note requires the old chain's files to remain on disk, unreachable but not deleted -- 'parked, not dead'. This is the concrete SUPERSEDES-without-history-loss case A-0803 asks for: the old claim is never deleted from claim.db, only superseded, exactly as the old runtime files are never deleted from the repo, only parked.

claims.normalized_claim: index.html boots the SHADED image-to-world engine directly via runtime/shaded-engine.mjs and its sibling runtime/integration scripts.
claims.subject: index.html boot chain

sources.original_text: index.html currently boots /src/main.js -- Snowflow, a WebGPU-only Babylon.js world-sandbox game -- not the runtime/*.mjs chain described below. This has been true since commit ec32657.

evidence.details: tools/test-single-canonical-ui.mjs directly asserts index.html's single script tag imports /src/main.js as a module.

tools/verify-no-legacy-ui.mjs asserts runtime/shaded-engine.mjs (and its sibling parked-engine files) still exist on disk -- the supersession did not delete the old chain, satisfying A-0803's 'ohne History-Verlust'.

relations.rationale: Commit ec3265749dd2648d74327bbc51ef8d21648a0c88 ('Drop in Snowflow as SHADED's runtime appearance (1:1 import)') is the explicit maintainer decision that replaced index.html's boot chain. C-BOOT-0001-OLD is NOT deleted or overwritten in claim.db -- it remains queryable as the historical fact it was, exactly as runtime/shaded-engine.mjs itself remains on disk, parked rather than deleted. This is A-0803's own requirement: supersession without history loss.
